notes: he that is distributed as the article's substantivizing rendering (rule 41) with the copula going to the predicate noun kohen (rule 20); an alternative would put he that is whole on kohen and give the written the to the first article, which rule 47's count then makes harder to justify.

The competing reading is rule 47's own case: ha-kohen ha-gadol renders as the high priest with the noun's article taking the single written the and the adjective's agreement article unrepresented, leaving he that to be placed elsewhere. It was rejected because rule 41's closing summary treats a supplied pronoun with a relative as the article's own rendering, which then leaves only the second article to take the written the.
mille' 'et-yado is treated as a single idiomatic unit under rule 30 rather than as one rendered verb beside three unrepresented tokens.
'asher plus the resumptive suffix on ro'sho is fused on whose under rules 22 and 30, exactly as 'asher bo is on wherein.
